scores.evidence: PRs come from forks, so CI runs without secrets and first-time-contributor workflow approval stays on
scores.rationale: Mostly accurate on GitHub mechanics (fork PR secrets, App permissions, at-least-once webhooks), with minor imprecision such as the rate limit stated as a 'requirement' and no mention of the GitHub App's limitation on pushing to forks or the cross-fork draft PR constraints.

scores.evidence: I assume it means "open a draft PR for human review." If you want auto-merge, that adds an R3 gate and a later phase
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolve, resolves ambiguity sensibly, explicit deferrals with reasons, and a buildable phased path.

scores.evidence: All GitHub writes go through a separate **executor** that holds the App key and accepts only typed actions
scores.rationale: Trust boundary, executor, sandbox, fork org and per-repo scoping are applied consistently across decisions, phases and cross-cutting tables.

scores.evidence: Injection suite of ≥100 cases planted in issue bodies, comments, repo files, tool output and test output
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, riskiest (trust boundary) early, replay evals, shadow mode, canary, and thresholds labeled as assumptions; ongoing CI and production metrics.

scores.evidence: I assume public repos with outside authors, the worst case. If the repos are internal only, the order stays the same and V3 gets easier.
scores.rationale: Assumptions, unknowns and baselines are labeled (ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN/CONFIRMED), with revisit triggers and sensitivity.

scores.evidence: Text planted in an issue, comment, repo file or test output takes over the agent. It then either (a) leaks secrets or private code
scores.rationale: Domain-specific failures (injection, exfiltration, backdoor PRs, cross-repo leak, bot interaction, dropped webhooks, runaway loops) with detection and recovery; minor gaps on mid-work issue edits.

scores.evidence: Terraform plus a GitHub Actions pipeline deploy pinned image digests. Rollback means redeploying the previous digest.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, alerts, pause drills and per-phase rollback are concrete; on-call ownership and incident response are thin ('business-hours on-call').

scores.evidence: Triage: ≤30k tokens and ≤$0.30 per issue. Fix attempt: ≤$8, ≤50 tool calls, ≤45 min
scores.rationale: Caps, monthly ceiling, cost per merged PR, build vs buy and routing are covered with labeled assumptions, but there is no bottom-up cost estimate and the sandbox/infra/people cost is largely absent.

scores.evidence: | Trust boundary and where credentials live | R3: a leaked secret can't be taken back |
scores.rationale: Decisions are classified by reversibility, validated early, with revisit triggers, exit paths, and model seam isolation.

scores.evidence: 3 deployables (agent service, action executor, sandbox pool) plus a queue and Postgres; business-hours on-call
scores.rationale: Mostly justified, with the split forced by the trust boundary; some ceremony (reversibility tags, phased routing, fork org, buy comparison) is heavy but defensible.

scores.evidence: Tasks, widest impact first: 1. Trust boundary: network-denied sandbox, registry proxy, no credentials inside, fork org (V1).
scores.rationale: Phased build with dependencies, concrete first slice, checkable exit criteria, and fallback actions if checks fail.

checklist.evidence: Comments always need approval ... The agent never merges, approves, closes PRs, or edits `.github/workflows`
The App has no `workflows`, `administration` or merge rights.
Issues, comments, repo files and tool output are data. Tool allow-list; typed actions; URL, image and path filters
throwaway sandbox (gVisor/Firecracker) with **no GitHub token and no cloud credentials**. Network is denied by default
scored against the fix PR's tests; Fork PRs without secrets; secret scanning on diffs
Precision ≥90% for each auto-applied label class; duplicate detection precision ≥80%
Cost per merged PR, review time and outcome metrics; ≥30% merged with only minor edits
caps cut runaway loops; Executor fails closed; pause drill run; kill switch
Append-only audit log of every action and approval
Code search in the sandbox (ripgrep plus a symbol index)
Webhook redelivery plus idempotency keys; dead-letter queue; polling sweep

traps.evidence: no GitHub token and no cloud credentials
Issue text goes in as a delimited data block, never as instructions.
Cost per merged PR ≤ the owner's target

note: Exceptionally strong, security-first phased plan with explicit validation gates and reversibility reasoning; weaker on cost grounding, incident ownership, and mid-work event handling.
